parsed.explanation: The parent regime imposes universal, traveller-facing exposures the division cannot remove: passports/visas must reflect sex assigned at birth, X markers are blocked, officers may refuse applications on any document 'discrepancy' with possible lifetime fraud findings, reported confiscations stranding travellers, national facility/custody rules including documented abuse of trans detainees, and foreign-government travel advisories. These apply at every entry and detention event regardless of the state's own law. The state/province layer, however, is genuinely protective: an independent July 2026 assessment places it in its low-risk tier; gender-identity discrimination is banned with a functioning commission awarding remedies; X licences and marker changes exist; the largest city is a declared sanctuary shielding travellers' care access; no bathroom ban, no sports restriction enacted (repeatedly vetoed/stalled); sodomy laws repealed. That is a documented territory-specific mitigation of the same order as the exposures, so per rule 12 the score sits above the parent's own (~0.45) but cannot reach the 0.75 band because the federal border, visa-fraud and custody exposures follow every visitor. 0.62 balances working local protection against an unremedied national universal-exposure regime.
